paper_metadata.title: The Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Refractory High-Entropy Alloys with High Plasticity

evidence.quote: Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) are promising materials used at high temperature, but their low plasticity restricts their application.

In this paper, four kinds of RHEAs with high plasticity (ZrTiHfV 0.5Nb0.5, Zr 2.0TiHfVNb2.0, ZrTiHfNb0.5Mo0.5, and ZrTiHfNb 0.5Ta0.5) were designed by controlling the VEC, and they were synthesized via vacuum arc melting in order to certify the accuracy of the VEC principle.

The ingots of four kinds of RHEAs were prepared by arc melting under a purified argon atmosphere. The cooling system employed a water-cooled copper crucible. Due to the high melting point of these alloys, relatively large current (350–450 A) and voltage (12–15 V) were used in the melting process. The low-melting metals were placed lower at the bottom and the ingots were remelted at least six times, which guaranteed the homogeneity of the composition.

attributes.morphology: primary dendrites intersect with secondary dendrites; network distribution

evidence.quote: Four kinds of RHEAs display dendritic structures, but each composition has a different morphology. In Figure 2a, the primary dendrites intersect with secondary dendrites, and the dendrites are distributed as a network in the high-magnification images.

attributes.morphology: secondary dendrites grow from both sides of the primary dendrites

evidence.quote: As shown in Figure 2b, the secondary dendrites grow from both sides of the primary dendrites, and some dendrites have a large size in the after-solidified region.
The microstructure of the ZrTiHfNb0.5Mo0.5 alloy displays reticulate dendrites in Figure 2c, which is beneficial to plasticity and strength.

attributes.morphology: relatively large dendrite structure; dendrites not connected; secondary dendrites perpendicular to primary dendrite

evidence.quote: Figure 2d demonstrates the relatively large dendrite structure of the ZrTiHfNb0.5Ta0.5 alloy. The dendrites are not connected, and the secondary dendrites are perpendicular to the primary dendrite, leading to the low strength of these alloys.

attributes.morphology: as-cast dendrites display a streamline structure; secondary dendrites tend to be paralleled to primary dendrites

evidence.quote: The original grain was compressed, and a small amount of equiaxial grains gathered along the direction of the deformation, which is a typical fracture after a high-temperature compression.
